recentItems.title: Brazil votes in a bitter election dominated by crime and corruption
recentItems.description:
The two main candidates in Brazil's presidential elections have both boycotted a TV debate ahead of the first round of voting on Sunday. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Current president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, and Flavio Bolsonaro, son of Lula's predecessor, are the only candidates with a real chance of winning. 

We’ve been out on the campaign trail in an election that's a story of left versus far-right, corruption and revenge, where powerful narco gangs are driving the agenda.

recentItems.title: G7 to release up to 100 million barrels of oil as diesel hits £2 a litre
recentItems.description:
G7 leaders have bowed to Donald Trump's demands, agreeing to release up to 100 million barrels of their diesel and crude oil reserves within four months. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The US President had threatened to cut US diesel exports if they didn't - keen to bring down fuel prices for voters ahead of next month's mid-term elections. 

Prices continue to rise here too - diesel reaching an average of two pounds a litre today for the first time.

recentItems.title: Mass protests escalate across France over school conditions
recentItems.description:
Riot police have clashed with high school students across France, fires and tear gas filling the streets, as protests over classroom conditions rage on. 

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

They began in the Paris region last week, but spread quickly across the country, growing increasingly violent. 

Hundreds of school staff and students have been injured and some two thousand protesters arrested. 

And a warning, you may find some of the images disturbing.

recentItems.title: Manchester City appeals guilty verdict over Premier League financial breaches
recentItems.description:
Manchester City has filed an appeal after an independent commission found it guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules over nine seasons.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

The club says it is innocent and the ruling contained "material errors of law, principle and fact".

The stakes are high, with point deductions or even relegation among the possible sanctions.

recentItems.title: Would be ‘silly’ to rule out coalition with Labour Party at next election, Polanski says
recentItems.description:
Green Party Leader Zack Polanski says it would be "silly” to rule out a coalition with the Labour Party at the next general election.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

Speaking to Channel 4 News at his party’s conference in Brighton, he says, “if a Labour government were ready to make the serious change that we needed, then of course my door would be open”.

recentItems.title: 'Houthi advances are major defeat for Saudi Arabia'
recentItems.description:
The Houthis have made rapid advances in Yemen, sparking a dormant civil war back to life in the Middle East, threatening their neighbour Saudi Arabia.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

We speak to the Iranian-American academic Vali Nasr about how the Islamist militia has become the key ally for Iran in its war with the US and Israel, and why the advances the group has made in Yemen represent a 'major strategic defeat' for Riyadh.

To learn more about why the Houthis success has global implications, watch our latest FourSight now.

recentItems.title: Is TikTok the future of local news?
recentItems.description:
As local news budgets shrink and misinformation spreads, independent creators are stepping up to keep communities informed.

[Subscribe to our Substack newsletter: https://channel4news.substack.com/subscribe]

With more than half a million followers, TikToker Andrew Barton is passionate about local journalism.

Channel 4 News asked him to investigate what the future of local news looks like and whether new government funding can help keep it alive.
